.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 148 PM EDT Wednesday...

There's some uncertainty with coverage of showers and storms 
tonight as some higher resolution models show we could miss out 
on rain as bulk of precipitation may pass to our north and 
south.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 308 PM EDT Wednesday...

1. Gusty south winds continue today. Widespread rainfall will 
move in this evening and overnight, with periods of moderate to 
locally heavy rain expected along with some embedded 
thunderstorms. 

2. Some scattered afternoon showers are possible each day 
Thursday through Saturday.

3. No significant weather Sunday through Wednesday. Moderating 
temperatures and dry weather expected early next week, then likely 
trending cooler with a low chance for showers.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 308 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Continue to expect some active weather this 
evening and overnight across the north country. A low pressure 
system passing north of our region will bring surface fronts 
across our area. Rain will move in from the west during the 
afternoon hours as a warm front approaches. Increasing southerly
flow is evident and will continue, especially over Lake 
Champlain where gusts over 30 kts have occurred and will 
continue into this evening. Lake Wind Advisory is in effect. 
Outside of Lake Champlain, highest gusts this afternoon will 
mainly be observed over the northern Champlain Valley, higher 
elevations of the Greens and Adirondacks, and over the northern 
slopes of the Adirondacks. Gusts will be strongest ahead of the 
steady rain, then will diminish as rain becomes widespread due 
to low-level stabilization. The increased southerly flow has 
bumped PWATS up to 1.5 to 2.0 inches, which is around 150 to 
200% of climatological normal for our area this time of year. 
This anomalously moist air mass will support some periods of 
moderate to heavy rain this evening into tonight. Models are 
indicating rates will mainly remain under a tenth of an inch an 
hour, but some heavier showers and thunderstorms could produce 
brief rainfall rates up to a quarter to a half inch an hour. 
Overall, the flood risk this evening into tonight is low (WPC's 
Excessive Rainfall Outlook has our entire area in a marginal 
risk of rainfall exceeding flash flood guidance). However, if 
any heavier storms track over the same area, those areas will 
need to be watched closely. In addition to moderate to briefly 
heavy rainfall, some thunderstorms are anticipated this evening 
into early tonight. The surface based instability and overall 
severe threat will be limited by a maintained low level 
inversion over most areas. However, the environment is slightly 
more favorable over the southern Saint Lawrence Valley, where 
the development of some marginal SBCAPE is progged. The amount 
of surface based instability is still somewhat in question, but 
latest SPC Convective Outlook maintains the Marginal Risk for 
most of Saint Lawrence County, with the Slight Risk just 
clipping our area and extending to the southwest. The main 
threat from thunderstorms in northern New York will be gusty 
winds and locally heavy rainfall. The remainder of our forecast 
area remains within the General Thunder contour, and risk of 
severe weather outside of the Saint Lawrence Valley is low 
tonight. There are some indications from higher resolution 
models that coverage of showers could be lower than anticipated 
with our region becoming split between an area of showers 
passing to our north while another passes to our south where the
better instability exists.

KEY MESSAGE 2: An upper level low in the area will keep chances
for showers each afternoon continuing from Thursday through 
Saturday. Temperatures will be a bit cooler than seasonal 
normals with periods of instability-driven afternoon showers. 
Coverage of showers will be greatest over higher terrain. 
Meanwhile, the Champlain Valley and Saint Lawrence Valley will 
remain mainly dry during this timeframe.

KEY MESSAGE 3: As the big upper level low continues to depart
slowly to the east Sunday in an Omega block pattern, the storm 
track behind it is favored to remain to our north with the upper
level ridge suppressed to our south. As a result, we will be in
a fairly dry northwest flow pattern through the middle of next 
week. There is very good clustering of temperatures and lack of 
precipitation on Sunday and Monday. Temperatures should warm 
from slightly below normal to near normal. 

Much larger spread in temperatures and dew points is noted after
that time, associated with the possibility of a surface cold 
front passing through from the north on Tuesday, which could 
bring substantially cooler and drier air into the region along 
with some lighter variety showers. A similar degree of 
uncertainty exists Wednesday but with temperatures shifted a 
bit warmer with more guidance showing a return to southerly low 
level flow. No huge swings in temperature are expected in this 
pattern, but fluctuations are possible.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 18Z Thursday...Scattered to overcast clouds with bases 
in the 2500 to 4000 feet range are generally expected over the 
next six hours. Aside from a shower in the vicinity of MSS at 
issuance time, no precipitation is expected until about 22-00Z.
Showers will increase in coverage from the west towards 00Z and
especially 02-06Z. These showers will be moderate to heavy at 
times, which will result in intervals of IFR visibility. While 
unlikely, some embedded thunderstorms are possible especially in
the vicinity of MSS. Ceilings will tend to lower to low 
MVFR/IFR levels after 06Z as moisture is trapped below a 
strengthening low level inversion following the exit of these 
showers, but a shift in winds towards the west during the 12Z to
18Z period will help improve conditions.

Winds currently are 10 to 15 knots with gusts 20 to 25 knots 
out of the south or southeast at most terminals, except under 
10 knots at MSS. Some LLWS is likely when surface winds weaken
as the aforementioned jet strengthens, primarily outside of the
Champlain Valley and from 03Z to 08Z.

Outlook...

Thursday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Friday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Friday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Saturday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Labor Day: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 219 PM EDT Wednesday...South winds 20 to 30 knots 
continue into this evening. Waves will build to 2 to 4+ feet by 
late tonight. Winds will be strongest this evening into the 
early overnight hours, then will decrease once steady rain 
develops. Winds on Thursday will be 15 to 20 knots in the 
morning, then become light and variable later in the day.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
